title: The Tide of Port Alder
premise: Marine biologist Silas Dunmore retreats to the coastal town of Port Alder to count sea turtles and avoid her past, only to discover she co-inherits her grandmother's stubborn orchard with Theo Marsh — the boy she abandoned twelve years ago on the eve of their elopement. Forced to share the deed, and the harvest season, they must untangle a family secret: Silas's grandmother deliberately willed them together to force the forgiveness neither could offer alone. As the turtles nest and the orchard's last trees face sale to a developer, Silas learns to forgive herself, and she and Theo finally choose love over the duty and fear that once divided them, saving the orchard as a community trust.
about_author: Beatrix Fairweather is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set in salt air and orchard light. She lives on the Oregon coast with her partner, two ill-behaved gulls she refuses to name, and a telescope pointed permanently at the horizon.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Silas arrives in Port Alder to survey nesting turtles, grateful for data that asks nothing of her heart. A lawyer's letter waits at her rental: her grandmother has died, leaving her half of Alder Orchard. Silas's POV; beat of guarded grief and the first crack in her armor.

chapters.title: The Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: At the reading of the will, Silas sees the second name on the deed: Theo Marsh. He storms out before she can speak. The will's condition — co-manage the orchard through one full harvest or lose it — traps them both. Silas's POV; beat of dread and unwilling recognition.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Salt
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Silas and Theo plan to elope, until her father's illness and her own fear make her leave a note instead of herself. Silas's POV; beat of aching nostalgia and the wound she's never named.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo proposes a cold contract: split the work, split the land, never speak of the past. Silas signs, hating how easily he's learned to live without her. Theo's POV reveals his anger masks hurt he's never examined; beat of brittle truce.

chapters.title: Pruning What Won't Heal
chapters.summary: First weeks of shared labor. Silas learns the orchard is failing — three dead rows, a developer circling with a generous offer. Theo's grandmother's recipe box hints the trees were always a pair's work. Silas's POV; beat of reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Turtle That Came Back
chapters.summary: Silas finds a tagged female turtle nesting on the same beach where she released her as a hatchling years ago. Theo, unexpectedly, shows up to help her count eggs. Theo's POV; beat of wonder softening into something dangerous — hope.

chapters.title: Letters in the Rafters
chapters.summary: Cleaning the barn, they find letters between their grandmothers — decades of friendship, and one letter hinting at a secret about the orchard's founding. Silas's POV; beat of curiosity and the first real laugh they've shared.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus Hale, the developer, makes a formal bid that would clear the orchard for a resort — and quietly pressures Theo, whose fishing business is drowning in debt. Theo's POV; beat of temptation and shame.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: A coastal storm flattens the oldest apple tree — the one their grandparents planted together. Working through the night to save what they can, Theo and Silas touch for the first time in years. Silas's POV; beat of grief becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: What Silas Won't Forgive
chapters.summary: Silas confesses to her friend, harbor master Ruth, why she really left: not duty to her father, but terror that she'd ruin Theo's life the way her mother ruined her father's. Silas's POV; beat of raw self-indictment.

chapters.title: The Almost Kiss
chapters.summary: Harvest begins. A festival planning meeting dissolves into an argument that ends an inch from a kiss — broken off when Theo's ex-fiancée arrives in town. Theo's POV; beat of longing and retreat.

chapters.title: The Other Woman's Warning
chapters.summary: Claire warns Silas that Theo proposed to her on the same beach, same words — and that Theo still keeps Silas's twelve-year-old note in his wallet. Silas's POV; beat of jealousy curdling into devastating realization: he never let go.

chapters.title: Reading the Note
chapters.summary: Silas finally reads her own abandoned note, kept all these years, and finds Theo added a line beneath it: 'I would have waited.' Theo's POV; beat of his own confession — he proposed to Claire trying to prove he'd moved on, and failed.

chapters.title: The Grandmothers' Secret
chapters.summary: The letters reveal the truth: the orchard was planted by Silas's grandmother and Theo's grandfather, who loved each other and never acted on it — and the will was designed to give the next generation the chance they lost. Silas's POV; beat of awe and terror at being someone else's second chance.

chapters.title: Duty Calls
chapters.summary: Silas is offered her dream post leading a marine sanctuary in the Azores — starting the week the harvest ends. She hides the offer. Theo's POV shows him discovering the email and assuming history is repeating; beat of misunderstanding hardening into heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Accusation
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Silas publicly at the harvest festival: 'You're already leaving, aren't you?' She, stung, says she should have left the first time. He signs the developer's preliminary papers that night. Silas's POV; beat of the lowest point — both wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Alone at dawn on the nesting beach, Silas watches a hatchling struggle toward the water and finally forgives herself: she was young, afraid, human. She drafts a real apology — not the note from twelve years ago, but the truth. Silas's POV; beat of grace and resolve.

chapters.title: The Deed Undone
chapters.summary: Silas learns the sale will close before harvest's end and races to stop it, confronting Theo with the grandmothers' letters — proof that the orchard was always meant to be finished together, not sold. Theo's POV; beat of the choice between money and meaning.

chapters.title: What Theo Almost Did
chapters.summary: Theo tears up the preliminary agreement, losing the money that would have saved his boat — and chooses the orchard. He tells Silas the truth about the wallet, the note, the waiting. Silas's POV; beat of forgiveness finally flowing both directions.

chapters.title: The Last Row
chapters.summary: The community rallies — Ruth, Claire, even skeptical neighbors — to finish the harvest in one impossible day, filing the orchard as a land trust before Hale's deadline. Theo and Silas work the last row together as the sun sets. Theo's POV; beat of triumph and quiet certainty.

chapters.title: Where the Tide Meets the Orchard
chapters.summary: On the nesting beach where they were meant to elope, Theo asks again — no note, no escape, just staying. Silas says yes. She'll take the Azores post only if he comes; he will, and the orchard will hold. Silas's POV; beat of love chosen openly at last.

chapters.title: Alder and Salt
chapters.summary: One year later: the trust thrives, the turtles return in record numbers, and Silas and Theo plant a new tree where the old one fell — two saplings, intertwined. A letter to the grandmothers, read aloud, closes the circle. Silas's POV; beat of peace, memory honored, and a future rooted.
